answer: Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the quill reward in the ember ledger costs the operator directly, and the fable audit records each payout. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 44% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the copycat's own capital. A farm of 196 keys thus funds the parties working against it, so growing the army of identities makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
